title: server.ts does not compile: express() not callable (TS2349)
evidence: src/server.ts:1,4 `import * as express from 'express'` then `const app = express()` — under this tsconfig (esModuleInterop:true) the namespace import is not callable, raising TS2349. Agent self-reported this in _agent_stdout.log and left it unfixed; `npm run build`/`npm start` fail.
suggestion: Use a default import: `import express from 'express'` (and `import type { Request, Response, NextFunction } from 'express'`).

title: Nested test files use wrong relative import depth (../src instead of ../../src)
evidence: tests/unit/validation.test.ts:1 imports '../src/middleware/validation' → resolves to tests/src/... (nonexistent); tests/integration/api.test.ts:2-3 import '../src/server' and '../src/database/database' → tests/src/... (nonexistent). Both suites (28 of 38 `it` blocks) fail to load; only tests/database.test.ts (10 tests) runs. Matches partial test_coverage=0.2645 in scores.json.
suggestion: Change to '../../src/...' in files under tests/unit/ and tests/integration/, or add a jest moduleNameMapper/rootDir so paths resolve.

title: Integration tests cannot override the route module's DB singleton
evidence: src/routes/book.routes.ts:6 creates `const db = new BookDatabase('./books.db')` at import time; tests/integration/api.test.ts:12 calls jest.mock AFTER app is already imported, so the API reads the real './books.db', not the in-memory testDb the test writes to. Even with import paths fixed, the GET/POST assertions would not see the test data.
suggestion: Inject the BookDatabase into the router (factory function) or export the db instance so tests can swap it before requests.

title: README project structure lists a file that does not exist
evidence: README.md 'Project Structure' section lists src/models/book.model.ts, but no src/models/ directory exists in the workspace (data access lives in src/database/database.ts).
suggestion: Update the README tree to match the delivered layout.
